text: first download raw IDAT files GEO retrieve sample metadata. GEO provides supplementary files series single tar archive (GSE250556_RAW.tar) containing gzipped IDAT files, read_idats() can import directly without decompressing .
code: data_dir = "GSE250556_RAW" dir.create(data_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)  # Download and unpack the archive of raw IDAT files (~1.1 GB) if (length(list.files(data_dir, pattern = "\\.idat(\\.gz)?$")) == 0) {   tar_file = file.path(data_dir, "GSE250556_RAW.tar")   options(timeout = max(3600, getOption("timeout"))) # large file   download.file(     "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/download/?acc=GSE250556&format=file",     method = "libcurl", destfile = tar_file,     mode = "wb")   untar(tar_file, exdir = data_dir)   file.remove(tar_file) # delete the archive to save disk space } #> [1] TRUE # 1. Fetch metadata from GEO pheno_url = "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE250556&targ=gsm&form=text&view=brief" pheno = readLines(pheno_url) pheno = split(pheno, cumsum(stringr::str_detect(pheno, "^\\^SAMPLE = GSM"))) names(pheno) = purrr::map_chr(pheno, 1) |> stringr::str_extract("GSM\\d+")  pheno_df = pheno |>   purrr::map(tibble::tibble) |>   dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "gsm") |>   tidyr::separate_wider_delim(2, delim = " = ", names = c("var", "val"),     too_many = "merge", too_few = "align_start") |>   dplyr::filter(var == "!Sample_title") |>   dplyr::mutate(subject_id = stringr::str_extract(val, "subject[A-Z]"))  # 2. Find local IDAT files idats = list.files(data_dir, pattern = "_Grn\\.idat(\\.gz)?$", full.names = TRUE) files_df = tibble::tibble(   prefix = stringr::str_remove(idats, "_Grn\\.idat(\\.gz)?$"),   gsm = stringr::str_extract(basename(prefix), "^GSM\\d+"))  # Merge metadata with local files pheno_df = dplyr::inner_join(pheno_df, files_df, by = "gsm", unmatched = "error") # 3. Read IDAT files meth = ewastools::read_idats(pheno_df$prefix, quiet = TRUE) #> [1] 1051943

code: pheno = pheno[,.(     gsm    ,sex = factor(sex, levels = c("m", "f")) # first level is the reference    ,smoking = factor(smoking, levels=c("non-smoker", "smoker"))    ,NE, MO, B, EO, BA, NK )] f = function(cpg){     m = lm(cpg ~ 1 + sex + smoking + NE + MO + B + EO + BA + NK, data=pheno)     coef(summary(m))["smokingsmoker", 4] # extract the p-value for the smoking }  f = purrr::possibly(f,otherwise=NA_real_) # catch errors  pvals = apply(beta, 1, f) SMK = na.omit(data.table(probe_id=rownames(beta), pval=pvals)) SMK[, qval := p.adjust(pval, m="fdr")] SMK = SMK[qval < 0.05] print(SMK) ##       probe_id         pval        qval ##         <char>        <num>       <num> ##  1: cg06882199 7.348569e-07 0.039618668 ##  2: cg01940273 1.389297e-08 0.002247054 ##  3: cg05951221 2.380479e-07 0.019250971 ##  4: cg21566642 7.874678e-09 0.002247054 ##  5: cg05575921 4.688252e-08 0.005687096 ##  6: cg14580211 2.051527e-07 0.019250971 ##  7: cg21161138 1.162694e-08 0.002247054 ##  8: cg25845688 1.247851e-06 0.049582165 ##  9: cg16571007 9.630933e-07 0.046731311 ## 10: cg02610360 1.161149e-06 0.049582165 ## 11: cg03099988 3.273600e-07 0.019855241 ## 12: cg16497398 1.328401e-06 0.049582165 ## 13: cg03636183 3.261651e-07 0.019855241

text: call_genotypes() calls genotypes SNP probes array detects outlying observations. mixture model (three Beta distributions representing genotypes AA, AB BB, one uniform distribution representing outliers) fitted beta-values SNP probes. title: Detection p-values — detectionP
text: Detection p-values assess whether signal given probe significantly different background noise. detectionP() recommended approach generates realistic p-values described Heiss Just, 2019. estimates background signal based opposite signal completely methylated completely unmethylated probes. detectionP.neg() follows approach used GenomeStudio, computes p-values based intensities negative control probes (yielding unrealistically small p-values). detectionP.minfi() provides implementation RGChannelSet objects used minfi package. eval_detP_cutoffs() generates plot showing number undetected chrY probes among male female subjects various p-value thresholds, order empirically choose threshold. Finally, mask() masks observations detection p-values specified threshold, .e., sets corresponding intensities M U NA.
